calls.reason: JLL supports development at a tens-of-gigawatts scale, but neither it nor Rystad ties that pipeline to $380 billion in required annual revenue. Rystad models a different revenue layer and scope.
Figma reported 48% revenue growth after Claude Design launched, but one quarter cannot settle whether Anthropic can displace it. The packet contains no sustained competitive-displacement evidence.

Reuters supports the roughly half-of-backlog figure, but future funding dependence remains unsettled. The S-1 summary reports an Anthropic operating profit, leaving the broader claim mixed rather than established.

AISI demonstrated substantial autonomous cyber capabilities in Mythos, but its tests do not settle the surrounding claims about broad white-collar automation. The claimed promotional motive also remains unproven.

The September coding study reports refusals or recognition of impossibility on 27% of unsatisfiable prompts. Failures remained common, but that directly undermines the categorical claim that coding models never acknowledge infeasibility.

CB&C reports $49.7 billion in private construction spending, raising doubts about $178.5 billion, but coverage is narrower and unreconciled. The packet does not establish the comparison with dot-com investment assumptions.
